v1_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume has roughly doubled since August 2026, from a ~600/month Jun-Jul baseline to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep (E-04); the dominant driver is a billing-accuracy defect in the import/validation processing of ACTUAL (non-estimated) meter reads, since 59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) carry read_type ACTUAL rather than ESTIMATED (E-01) and a tariff-rate change has been ruled out as that defect's cause (E-02, E-06).
v2_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-04). Current evidence confirms that billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 to compare raw AMI register values against 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-13), combined with firmware v4.2 meters (rollout 2026-06) reporting register values in 0.1 m3 units instead of m3 (E-14), causes legitimate high-consumption rejections (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) that reproduce in 1184 of 1240 (95.5%) disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-12, E-15). E-16 confirms this defect is confined to the ESTIMATED-read minority (1240/3025, 41%): the 1184 affected accounts it identified are all ESTIMATED read type with zero ACTUAL, so a separate, as-yet-unidentified billing-import mechanism must account for the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (59%, the majority of the surge).
